steps.prompt: Look back at Mock A. Which one change will you make to how you take Mock B?

cards.title: Same plan, better execution
cards.body: Use the same pacing plan as in Mock A, with the one change you picked. Watch the clock at problem $10$ (about $20$ minutes in) and at problem $20$. Before you hand in, check that every answer is the letter you meant.

cards.title: Mistake analysis
cards.body: After the mock, open your result and sort every miss and blank into one of four boxes: (1) I didn't know the idea, (2) a careless slip, (3) I misread the question, (4) I ran out of time. Add the problems you didn't know to your error log, and look at the review by strand and by difficulty: is one strand weak, or do the points leak away in the last ten problems?

cards.title: Compare the two mocks
cards.body: Put the results side by side: the score, how many blanks, and which of the four boxes your misses fell into. One mock is a snapshot; two show a direction. Your progress page shows your AMC-score estimate from your last full tests.

prompts: Did your change from Mock A work?
Which strand cost you the most points this time?
